ai.description: This lizard reaches 12–15 cm snout-vent length. It is grey-brown with dark dorsal blotches and a bright yellow or orange throat in males. It features a flattened body and granular scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Paralaudakia himalayana* by the presence of a distinct, enlarged, and often spiny patch of scales on the sides of the neck, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Himalayan Agama inhabits rocky, arid slopes and boulder-strewn terrain within the high-altitude regions of the Himalayas, typically ranging from 2,000 to 4,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan Agama is a diurnal lizard that frequently basks on sun-drenched rocks to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for insects and plant matter.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Paralaudakia himalayana* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, generally from May to July.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Paralaudakia himalayana* inhabits the high-altitude regions of the Western Himalayas, specifically across Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand, at elevations of 2,500–4,500m.
